questions.title: When do you need to drop the ball again?
questions.question: You try to drop your ball, but it hits your leg or your bag before it hits the ground. What should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball where it is
Add a penalty and keep playing

questions.explanation: If your ball touches you or your things before it touches the ground, you have to drop it again. There is no penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Letting the ball fall from your hand at your knee so it can land and stop.
Things you use to play golf, like your clubs, bag, and trolley.

questions.teachingTip: Show children how to drop a ball from knee height and remind them to stand clear of their bag and feet.
likelyMisconceptions: They might think they should keep playing if the ball touches them or their things.
They might think they get a penalty even if they drop again.

questions.title: When must a ball be dropped again?
questions.question: If you drop the ball but it touches you or your equipment before hitting the ground, what must you do?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies
Add a penalty and play on

questions.explanation: If the dropped ball touches you or your equipment before hitting the ground, you must drop it again without penalty.
